key_insight: Nose bluntness and wall temperature control hypersonic boundary-layer receptivity by jointly setting the stagnation vorticity response and the downstream lift-up amplification.
engineering_relevance: The results provide scaling laws that can help predict and manage transition in hypersonic blunt-nose vehicles by tuning geometry and wall thermal conditions.
method: Three-step asymptotic receptivity model linking free-stream forcing to downstream perturbations
Seven case studies varying Reynolds number (nose bluntness) and wall temperature
evidence_signal: The abstract reports detailed analysis across seven cases and derives explicit scaling laws for receptivity efficiency with respect to nose bluntness and wall temperature.
watch_item: The conclusions rely on asymptotic modeling and linearized analysis, so applicability may be limited when strong nonlinear effects or real-flight uncertainties become important.
paper_title: Excitation of non-modal perturbations in hypersonic boundary layers by free stream forcing. Part III: effects of wall temperature and nose bluntness
